findings.title: Path Traversal Open
findings.description: The current implementation is vulnerable to path traversal attacks because it only uses os.path.basename to strip directory paths, but does not prevent filenames containing '..' or '/'. To fix this, we need to add additional validation to prevent such filenames. This can be achieved by checking for '..' or '/' in the filename and returning an error if found.
findings.cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
findings.fix_hint: Validate and sanitize the filename to prevent path traversal attacks
findings.fixed_code: filename = os.path.basename(filename); if '..' in filename or filename.startswith('/'): return 'Invalid filename'; with open(os.path.join('/var/data', filename)) as f: return f.read()

findings.title: Security group allows unrestricted SSH (port 22)
findings.description: The security group allows unrestricted access to port 22, which is a critical vulnerability. To fix this, we need to restrict the ingress rule to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks. By updating the security group resource, we can limit the exposure to only trusted sources.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the security group to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks

findings.title: Aws Db Instance No Logging
findings.description: The AWS DB instance is missing logging configuration, which can cause important event information to be lost. Enabling logging by setting 'enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports' will allow the instance to export logs to CloudWatch. This will provide visibility into database events and help with auditing and troubleshooting.
findings.cwe: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
findings.fix_hint: Enable logging for the AWS DB instance by setting the 'enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports' argument
findings.fixed_code:
resource "aws_db_instance" "app_db" {
  identifier          = "app-db"
  engine              = "mysql"
  instance_class      = "db.t3.micro"
  username            = "admin"
  password            = var.db_password
  publicly_accessible = false
  storage_encrypted   = true
  enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports = ["error", "general", "slowquery"]
}

findings.title: S3 versioning disabled
findings.description: The CKV_AWS_21 check failed because S3 versioning was not enabled on the bucket, which can lead to data loss in case of accidental deletion or overwrite. Enabling versioning allows for the storage of multiple versions of an object, enabling recovery of previous versions. This can be achieved by adding the versioning block to the aws_s3_bucket resource in the Terraform configuration.
findings.fix_hint: Enable versioning on the S3 bucket to track changes and prevent data loss

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: ec2:*
findings.description: The current policy allows full EC2 control, which is a security risk. To fix this, the policy should be updated to only include the specific EC2 actions required by the application. For example, if the application only needs to describe instances, the policy should be restricted to ec2:DescribeInstances.
findings.fix_hint: Remove or restrict the overly permissive ec2:* action to only include necessary EC2 actions

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: s3:*
findings.description: The current policy allows full S3 access on all buckets, which is a security risk. The fixed policy restricts S3 access to only the 'my-app-data' bucket and only allows 'GetObject' and 'PutObject' actions. This reduces the attack surface and follows the principle of least privilege.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the 's3:*' action with specific actions required by the application, such as 's3:GetObject' and 's3:PutObject', and restrict the resource to the specific bucket 'my-app-data'

attack_chains.title: EC2 Instance Compromise
attack_chains.description: An attacker gains access to an EC2 instance with a public IP, then uses a security group allowing unrestricted SSH to gain control of the instance. This gives them access to sensitive data and the ability to move laterally within the network.
steps: Step 1: attacker accesses EC2 instance with public IP using finding b5d39f8b in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf
Step 2: attacker uses security group allowing unrestricted SSH (finding 52159918 in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf) to gain control of the instance
attack_chains.remediation: Remove public IP from EC2 instance

attack_chains.title: S3 Data Exfiltration
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses a dangerous IAM action to access S3, then exploits S3 access logging being disabled to exfiltrate sensitive data without detection. This gives them access to sensitive data and the ability to move laterally within the network.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses dangerous IAM action (finding be083391 in file iam/policy.json) to access S3
Step 2: attacker exploits S3 access logging being disabled (finding a7b892f0 in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf) to exfiltrate sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Remove dangerous IAM action for S3 access

attack_chains.title: Path Traversal and EC2 Compromise
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses a path traversal vulnerability in the code to access sensitive data, then uses a security group allowing unrestricted SSH to gain control of an EC2 instance. This gives them access to sensitive data and the ability to move laterally within the network.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses path traversal vulnerability (finding cf32085e in file src/app.py) to access sensitive data
Step 2: attacker uses security group allowing unrestricted SSH (finding 52159918 in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf) to gain control of an EC2 instance
